The key to a strong and stable structure lies beneath the surface. Let’s dig into the fascinating world of footings! 🔍 🌐 Footing Fundamentals: Footing is the unsung hero of construction, responsible for transferring the weight of a building to the solid ground below. It’s a game-changer! But how do you choose the right type of footing? 🤔 ✅ Factors to Consider: 1️⃣ Depth of Safe-Bearing Strata 2️⃣ Soil Type & Condition 3️⃣ Superstructure’s Needs 🏠 Isolated Footing: When you’ve got single columns standing solo, isolated footings are your go-to choice. These footings ensure stability, prevent sinking, and keep things safe and sound. 💰 Cost-Effective Choice: Isolated footings are often the budget-friendly option, especially when the ground’s properties remain consistent. Now, let’s talk types of isolated footings: 1️⃣ Pad Footing: Versatile in shape, efficient, but watch out for lateral forces! What’s your preference – circular, rectangular, or square? 2️⃣ Sloped Footing: Less concrete, less reinforcement, and a sleek 45-degree slope. It’s all about maintaining that perfect angle! 📐 3️⃣ Stepped Footing: A classic approach for residential buildings, although it’s become less common in recent years. 🏘️ 4️⃣ Combined Footing: When space is tight, and individual footings won’t cut it, we combine forces! 💪 What’s your experience with footings? What gets checked before we pour concrete? On this ADU project, we’re preparing the attached garage footing for inspection. - Footing size and depth help provide the support shown in the structural plans. - Rebar reinforces the concrete, and proper placement keeps it surrounded by enough concrete to protect it. - Epoxied rebar connections tie the new footing into the existing foundation. Where required, a deputy inspector checks the installation before it gets covered. - Anchor bolts secure the garage’s wood framing to the concrete foundation. Their location, spacing, and embedment matter. For homeowners, this is why inspections before the pour are so important. These connections become hidden once the concrete is placed, so this is the time to verify that the work follows the approved plans.
